util

Class SmartDateParser

  • java.lang.Object
    • util.SmartDateParser

  • public final class SmartDateParser
extends java.lang.Object
    /** A flexible utility for converting date strings of varying formats into Date, LocalDateTime, and ZonedDateTime objects.

    Regional Support and Ambiguity: This parser is optimised for Australian/British (DD/MM/YYYY) date formats. In cases of numerical ambiguity, for example: 01/02/2026, the parser prioritises the Day-Month-Year interpretation (1st February).

    Supported Date Formats - Date Parsing Standards
    Standard Format Pattern / Example Description
    EXIF Standard yyyy:MM:dd HH:mm:ss Standard camera metadata format using colons as delimiters.
    ISO-8601 yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS Supports T delimited timestamps with optional sub-seconds.
    International/US MMM dd, yyyy or MMM dd yyyy Supports textual month patterns (e.g., Jan 19, 2026).
    Since:
    19 January 2026
    Version:
    1.2
    Author:
    Trevor Maggs

    • Method Detail

      • convertToDate

        public static java.util.Date convertToDate(java.lang.String input)
        Obtains a Date object after parsing the specified date input.

        This method is provided for backward compatibility with legacy APIs that require Date. For modern logic, convertToZonedDateTime(String) is preferred.

        Parameters:
        input - the date string to convert
        Returns:
        a Date object representing the parsed timestamp
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if the input is null or does not match any known date format

      • convertToZonedDateTime

        public static java.time.ZonedDateTime convertToZonedDateTime(java.lang.String input)
        Attempts to parse a raw date string into a ZonedDateTime object by matching it against a collection of supported date and time patterns.

        This method prioritises ISO-8601 full date-time formats before falling back to common regional patterns (e.g., Australian DD/MM/YYYY). If a pattern matches but lacks timezone data, the system's default ZoneId is applied.

        Parameters:
        input - the raw date string to be parsed, such as "23/04/2026" or "2026-04-23T20:00:00Z"
        Returns:
        a valid ZonedDateTime representing the input or null if the input is not defined correctly
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if the input does not match any known format

      • parseZonedISO_8601

        private static java.time.ZonedDateTime parseZonedISO_8601(java.lang.String input)
        Parses ISO-8601 strings with a preference for preserving existing offsets using DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME.
        Parameters:
        input - the ISO-8601 string
        Returns:
        a ZonedDateTime object; if no offset is present, the result is normalised to the system's default time zone.
